name: CVPR
fullName: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition
notes: Paper enrollment is mandatory. All authors need an OpenReview profile; profiles without an institutional email may take up to two weeks to activate. Main sessions June 22–25.

publication.note: No journal track announced in the linked call. Conference proceedings are distinct from a journal.

guide.contribution: Recent papers develop reusable visual models and inference methods, including controllable video generation and motion synthesis. Contributions isolate a concrete capability, such as separating camera and subject motion, then demonstrate how the method supports several visual tasks or input conditions.
guide.evidence: Evaluation combines quantitative comparisons with visual results and, for perceptual claims, human judgments. Motion work measures control and realism together, tests different inputs and applications, and compares against existing generation methods. Diverse outputs matter when a method claims to model multiple plausible futures.

comparisons.difference: CVPR and ICCV publish visual learning, video and 3D reconstruction. Recent CVPR generation papers measure motion control, realism and diversity; recent ICCV reconstruction papers measure image quality, view consistency and robustness to capture errors.

Recent CVPR work develops visual generation methods and tests control, realism and variation across inputs. Recent WACV work addresses operating constraints such as low light or unseen objects, testing pose accuracy and performance in the final application.

name: ICCV
fullName: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision
notes: ICCV 2027 event dates are announced, but its submission schedule was not published when checked. The 2025 schedule supplies the biennial estimate basis. Paper registration is mandatory.

publication.note: No journal track announced in the linked call. Conference proceedings are distinct from a journal.

guide.contribution: Recent reconstruction papers combine learned visual priors with explicit scene or sensor structure. They address concrete failures such as inconsistent views, fast motion or changing objects, and introduce methods that improve image recovery, camera estimation or persistent 3D scene representations.
guide.evidence: Experiments connect image quality or reconstruction accuracy to difficult capture conditions. Recent papers use synthetic and real scenes, compare competing reconstruction or interpolation methods, and test corruptions, motion and object changes. Visual sequences show whether the resulting representations remain coherent over time.

comparisons.difference: ICCV and CVPR publish visual learning, video and 3D reconstruction. Recent ICCV reconstruction work tests changing scenes and difficult capture conditions; recent CVPR generation work tests controllable motion, realistic appearance and output diversity.

Recent ICCV work evaluates recovered images and reconstructed scenes, including restoration under capture errors. 3DV puts the 3D output at the center: camera poses, point-cloud labels, preserved geometry and scene consistency.

name: ECCV
notes: Paper registration is mandatory. The submission uses Central European Time. Event dates include workshops September 8–9 and main conference September 10–12, as listed on the official Dates page.

publication.note: No journal track announced in the linked call. Conference proceedings are distinct from a journal.

guide.contribution: Recent papers improve visual models by introducing explicit structure into reconstruction or reasoning. Examples include consistent scenes from generated views, contact-aware human reconstruction and region-grounded image assessment. Each method identifies a failure of existing models and adds a mechanism that addresses it.
guide.evidence: Evaluation follows the claimed capability: geometric and contact metrics for reconstruction, robustness and generalization for assessment, and runtime for efficient inference. Comparisons include existing methods and varied scenes or inputs. Human judgments supplement metrics when visible plausibility is part of the contribution.

comparisons.difference: ECCV and ICCV publish learned reconstruction methods. Recent ECCV work tests human contact geometry and consistency of generated views; recent ICCV work tests fast motion, corrupted inputs and scene changes.

ECCV includes image assessment and visual reasoning as well as reconstruction. 3DV concentrates on 3D representations, with evaluations of camera poses, geometric preservation, reconstruction and point-cloud segmentation.

name: 3DV
notes: Submission and abstract share a deadline. The official page explicitly labels all other deadlines 11:00 am PDT, including December; this preserves the published offset. Verify notification timing with the organizers.

core.note: No matching entry found by acronym and full title; this is not an Unranked classification.

publication.note: No journal track announced in the linked call. Conference proceedings are distinct from a journal.

guide.contribution: Recent papers introduce 3D representations and algorithms for reconstruction, editing and scene understanding. Contributions directly address geometry: scaling scene recovery, preserving untouched shape during editing, or transferring image semantics into consistent point-cloud predictions. New benchmarks accompany tasks that lack suitable measurements.
guide.evidence: Evaluation measures the specific 3D output, including camera poses, novel views, preservation of geometry or point-cloud segmentation. Experiments span established datasets, compare relevant baselines and test efficiency or scale. Editing studies assess both the modified region and the consistency of the preserved structure.

comparisons.difference: 3DV evaluates geometric outputs such as camera poses, edited shapes and point-cloud labels. CVPR also publishes video generation, where motion control, visual realism and diversity can be the main results.

3DV tests the quality and consistency of a 3D representation. Recent WACV reconstruction and pose papers also ask whether that representation improves an application under constraints such as low light or unfamiliar objects.

name: ICRA
fullName: IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation
notes: The conference CFP extended the paper deadline to September 16 and explicitly states PST even in September; the published fixed offset is retained. The final-paper date is listed by IEEE RAS. Main contributed-paper track only.

journals: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering (T-ASE)
publication.note: Already accepted RAS journal articles may be presented. Conference submission does not itself publish in these journals.

guide.contribution: Recent papers connect perception, learning or control methods to specific robot capabilities. They address partial observations, difficult sensing conditions and deployment errors through algorithmic changes or integrated systems. Contributions explain how those changes improve a robot's estimation, manipulation or motion.
guide.evidence: Experiments combine relevant benchmarks with robot or sensor data and measure outcomes such as success, tracking error, accuracy and runtime. Recent work varies obstacles, sensing conditions or trajectories, compares baselines, and tests whether the proposed mechanism remains effective under those changes.

comparisons.difference: ICRA and IROS publish perception, control and robot systems tested in simulation and physical experiments. Recent ICRA work measures tracking and sensor-fusion accuracy; recent IROS work also tests actuator limits, navigation transfer and gripper behavior.

ICRA includes sensor fusion, state estimation and control, evaluated through tracking error, runtime and robot task success. CoRL centers on learning: evaluate training data, policy success and transfer to new tasks or objects.

name: IROS
fullName: IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems
notes: The paper date and event are published in the official IEEE Robotics and Automation Society calendar. A submission time, timezone, and remaining review milestones were not specified in that source.

publication.note: Accepted RA-L papers may transfer for presentation at IROS 2027 during August 1, 2026?April 30, 2027, subject to journal eligibility. This is journal-first publication, not a journal track within the conference paper submission.

guide.contribution: Recent papers improve robot operation through planning algorithms, adaptive navigation and mechanism design. They formulate practical constraints explicitly, such as actuator limits, unfamiliar environments or variable object surfaces, and develop methods or hardware that address the resulting performance bottleneck.
guide.evidence: Evaluation uses simulation and physical experiments matched to the contribution. Planning studies test feasibility and task efficiency, navigation studies compare robustness and training cost, and hardware studies verify analytical models and handling performance. Baselines and varied operating conditions make the benefit measurable.

comparisons.difference: IROS and ICRA publish integrated robot systems. Recent IROS work tests navigation in new environments, actuator constraints and gripping surfaces; recent ICRA work tests partial observations, tracking trajectories and sensor-fusion accuracy.

IROS includes hardware mechanisms and constrained planning, tested through physical behavior and task efficiency. CoRL focuses on learned policies and representations, tested through data efficiency, task success and generalization.

name: RSS
notes: New two-stage process for 2027: the December 4 extended abstract is compulsory and includes up to five pages of content plus one reference page. The April final-paper deadline is invitation-only after stage 1.

core.note: Older CORE edition; no ICORE2026 entry found.

publication.note: No journal track announced in the linked call. Conference proceedings are distinct from a journal.

guide.contribution: Recent papers develop focused robotics methods with a clear connection between the underlying mechanism and observed performance. Contributions range from demonstration synthesis and geometric optimization to odometry. They address specific limitations such as data collection cost, delayed communication or poorly constrained geometry.
guide.evidence: Evidence depends on the claim: robot trials test generalization across tasks, objects or platforms; optimization work combines analysis with benchmark comparisons; estimation work tests varied sensors and degenerate environments. Experiments connect improvements to the proposed mechanism and measure robustness or computational cost.

comparisons.difference: RSS and CoRL publish robot learning evaluated across tasks and platforms. RSS also includes geometric optimization and odometry, where convergence, communication delays and sensor accuracy can be the main results.

Recent RSS work tests specific mechanisms such as demonstration synthesis or distributed optimization across tasks and operating conditions. ICRA also publishes integrated perception and control systems, evaluated through tracking accuracy, runtime and robot task success.

name: CoRL
notes: The author guide explicitly confirms May 28 as the paper deadline. May 25 abstract date comes from the official CoRL Organization Board announcement; no time is asserted. Notification date comes from the archived official reviewer guide. Main conference November 9–11; workshops November 12.

publication.note: Papers publish in Proceedings of Machine Learning Research (PMLR), a proceedings series, not a journal track.

guide.contribution: Recent papers improve how robot policies learn from data, use sensory representations or are evaluated. Contributions include data-selection methods, multimodal tactile pretraining and distributed benchmarking. The central result connects a learning or evaluation design to improved behavior on robotic tasks.
guide.evidence: Experiments measure policy success, data efficiency and generalization in simulation or on real robots. Representation studies test downstream manipulation and state inference; evaluation studies compare policies across tasks and sites. Multiple conditions and direct policy comparisons establish whether improvements extend beyond a single setup.

comparisons.difference: CoRL focuses on how policies learn and transfer: measure training-data needs, task success and performance on new objects or tasks. ICRA also accepts contributions in hardware, sensor fusion and control, where the main improvement need not come from learning.

CoRL and RSS publish robot learning with task-success and generalization experiments. RSS also covers analytical optimization and state estimation, evaluated through convergence, sensor accuracy and computational cost.

name: WACV
fullName: IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision
topics: IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision
notes: Tracks the final submission round; new papers can enter either round. Round 1 enrollment/paper dates were June 19/26, 2026. Enrollment is mandatory. The official Dates page updates decisions to October 14; author guidelines retain October 9. Next-cycle estimates use round 2, not the earlier round. Exact clock time is not published on the dates page.

publication.note: No journal track announced in the linked call. Conference proceedings are distinct from a journal.

guide.contribution: Recent papers address concrete limitations of vision systems, including unseen-object pose estimation, extremely low illumination and reconstruction quality for downstream use. Contributions include new methods, targeted datasets and comparative studies that explain how a design choice affects an application.
guide.evidence: Experiments reproduce the stated operating constraint and measure task-level performance. Recent papers use synthetic and real data, compare established pipelines, and examine robustness to viewpoint or illumination. Comparative studies also measure runtime and test whether intermediate quality metrics predict the final task result.

comparisons.difference: Recent WACV pose and reconstruction papers test performance under practical sensing constraints and in the final application. 3DV more directly evaluates the representation itself: geometric accuracy, camera poses and consistency of 3D structure.

Recent WACV work measures vision performance under low light, unseen objects or limited capture data. Recent CVPR generation work measures how accurately users can control motion and how realistic and varied the generated videos are.
